source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Signs of Strength in a Breakout

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode. Chapter 2 gives a bull-breakout signs-of-strength list and states 'the opposite of all of the preceding is true for bear breakouts', so each bullet is mined once with sides=mirrored rather than twice.

candidates.name: BreakoutBarBodyDominance
candidates.quote: The breakout bar has a large bull trend body and small tails or no tails. The larger the bar, the more likely the breakout will succeed.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: the breakout bar is a large-bodied trend bar with small or no tails.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - open[0]) >= bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && (high[0] - close[0]) <= tailFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && (open[0] - low[0]) <= tailFraction * (high[0] - low[0])
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (bar classification used as a breakout-quality test)

complexity.reason: single-bar OHLC arithmetic

notes: Shared primitive for this chapter; reused by several other signs below.

candidates.name: BreakoutVolumeMultiple
candidates.quote: If the volume is 10 to 20 times the average volume of recent bars, the chance of follow-through buying and a possible measured move increases.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: the breakout bar's volume is a large multiple of the recent average.

complexity.reason: rolling average-volume window

candidates.name: SpikeBreaksMultipleResistanceLevels
candidates.quote: The spike goes very far, lasts several bars, and breaks several resistance levels like the moving average, prior swing highs, and trend lines, and each by many ticks.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: within the spike, price clears several distinct resistance levels (EMA, a swing high, a trend line) by more than a minimal margin.
candidates.pseudocode: levelsClearedByMargin(ema(emaLength)[0], highest(high, swingLookback)[1], trendLine[0], marginTicks * tickSize, spikeBars) >= minLevelsCleared

complexity.reason: needs an EMA, a swing-high window, and trend-line projection from pivots, all checked over a spike window

candidates.name: FollowThroughBarSize
candidates.quote: The next two or three bars also have bull bodies that are at least the average size of the recent bull and bear bodies ... if the follow-through bar is large, the odds of the trend continuing are greater.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: the bar(s) immediately after the breakout bar have with-trend bodies at least as large as the recent average body.
candidates.pseudocode: for i in 1..followThroughBars: close[i] > open[i] && (close[i] - open[i]) >= average(abs(close - open), bodyLookback)[i]

complexity.reason: fixed-length loop comparing bodies to a rolling average

candidates.name: SpikeLengthWithoutPullback
candidates.quote: The spike grows to five to 10 bars without pulling back for more than a bar or so.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: the spike runs for several bars with no pullback longer than one bar.

complexity.reason: a persistent counter tolerating brief interruptions

candidates.name: BreakoutClearsScalpDistance
candidates.quote: As a bull breakout goes above a prior significant swing high, the move above the high goes far enough for scalpers to make a profit if they entered on a stop at one tick above that swing high.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: price clears the breakout swing high by at least a scalper's-profit distance.
candidates.pseudocode: swingHigh = highest(high, swingLookback)[1]; high[0] - swingHigh >= scalpTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: a highest-high window plus a fixed distance check

candidates.name: SpikeBarLowNearPriorClose
candidates.quote: One or more bars in the spike has a low that is at or just one tick below the close of the prior bar.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: somewhere in the spike, a bar's low barely dipped below the prior bar's close (almost no give-back).
candidates.pseudocode: exists i in [0, spikeBars): low[i] <= close[i + 1] && low[i] >= close[i + 1] - toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: a fixed-length existence scan over two-bar comparisons

candidates.name: SpikeBarOpenAbovePriorClose
candidates.quote: One or more bars in the spike has an open that is above the close of the prior bar.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: somewhere in the spike, a bar gapped open above the prior close.
candidates.pseudocode: exists i in [0, spikeBars): open[i] > close[i + 1]

complexity.reason: a fixed-length existence scan

candidates.name: SpikeBarStrongClose
candidates.quote: One or more bars in the spike has a close on its high or just one tick below its high.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: somewhere in the spike, a bar closed at or within a tick of its own high.
candidates.pseudocode: exists i in [0, spikeBars): close[i] >= high[i] - toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: a fixed-length existence scan

candidates.name: MicroGapAfterTrendBar
candidates.quote: The low of the bar after a bull trend bar is at or above the high of the bar before the bull trend bar, creating a micro gap, which is a sign of strength.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: a three-bar micro gap forms around a trend bar — the bar following it never trades back into the range of the bar preceding it.

complexity.reason: a three-bar structural test built on the trend-bar primitive

notes: Same construction as chapter 1's TrailingStopInMicroMeasuringGap gap test (R01-03) and R08's gap family.

candidates.name: TrendResumptionContext
candidates.quote: The overall context makes a breakout likely, like the resumption of a trend after a pullback, or a higher low or lower low test of the bear low after a strong break above the bear trend line.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: the breakout occurs as a trend resumption or a higher-low test after a trend-line break, rather than in a neutral context.

complexity.reason: ‘overall context’ bundles several undefined pattern-recognition concepts

candidates.name: RecentStrongTrendDays
candidates.quote: The market has had several strong bull trend days recently.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: several of the recent daily bars qualify as strong trend days.

complexity.reason: ‘trend day’ needs a design decision, as in R08-24

candidates.name: TrendBarDominanceInRange
candidates.quote: There was growing buying pressure in the trading range, represented by many large bull trend bars, and the bull trend bars were clearly more prominent than the bear trend bars in the range.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: over the trading range preceding the breakout, bull trend bars clearly outnumber bear trend bars.

complexity.reason: a CountIF over a fixed window on a bar-classification series

candidates.name: FirstPullbackDelayed
candidates.quote: The first pullback occurs only after three or more bars of breaking out.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: no meaningful pullback occurs until at least N bars into the breakout.

complexity.reason: needs the breakout-start bar remembered as state and a pullback-detection routine

candidates.name: FirstPullbackShortDuration
candidates.quote: The first pullback lasts only one or two bars and it follows a bar that is not a strong bear reversal bar.
candidates.description: Sign of strength: the first pullback is brief and was not triggered by a strong reversal bar.

complexity.reason: needs pullback-span detection plus a reversal-bar primitive

candidates.name: FirstPullbackShallow
candidates.quote: The first pullback does not reach the breakout point and does not hit a breakeven stop (the entry price).
candidates.description: Sign of strength: the first pullback's low stays above both the breakout point and the entry price.

complexity.reason: needs the remembered breakout point and the position's entry price

candidates.name: BreakoutReversesManyBars
candidates.quote: this breakout bar has a high and close that are above the highs and closes of five or even 20 or more bars ... a close below a low is more of a sign of strength than simply a low that is below a prior low.
candidates.description: Sign of strength, graded by degree: count how many of the last N bars' highs and closes the breakout bar's close reverses; a close-based reversal count is a stronger sign than a high-based one.
candidates.pseudocode: closeReversedCount = count(i in [1, lookback]: close[0] > high[i]); highReversedCount = count(i in [1, lookback]: high[0] > high[i]); closeReversedCount >= minReversedBars

complexity.reason: a fixed window counted against a highest/lowest-style comparison

notes: Also captures the bar 26 example on page 44-45.

candidates.name: WeakBreakoutBarSmallBodyLargeTail
candidates.quote: The breakout bar has a small or average-size bull trend body and a large tail on top.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: the breakout bar has only a modest body and a prominent tail against the breakout direction.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - open[0]) < bodyFraction * (high[0] - low[0]) && (high[0] - close[0]) >= tailFraction * (high[0] - low[0])

complexity.reason: single-bar OHLC arithmetic

candidates.name: StrongBearReversalAfterBreakout
candidates.quote: The next bar has a bear body and is either a bear reversal bar or a bear inside bar; that bar closes on or near its low, and the body is about the size of the average bodies of the bars before the breakout ... The bar after the breakout bar is a strong bear reversal bar or a bear inside bar.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: the bar right after the breakout bar is a full-bodied bear reversal or inside bar closing near its low.
candidates.pseudocode: close[0] < open[0] && close[0] <= low[0] + nearLowTicks * tickSize && (open[0] - close[0]) >= average(abs(close - open), bodyLookback)[0]

complexity.reason: single-bar arithmetic against a rolling average body size

notes: The book states this point twice in the same list (p39 and p40); mined once.

candidates.name: UnfavorableRallyContext
candidates.quote: The overall context makes a breakout unlikely, like a rally to test the high of a trading range day, but the rally has bear bars, many overlapping bars, bars with prominent tails, and a couple of pullbacks along the way.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: the leg leading into the breakout already shows two-sided character (bear bars, overlap, tails, pullbacks).

complexity.reason: aggregates several undefined bar-quality measures into one judgment

candidates.name: PriorTradingRangeDays
candidates.quote: The market has been in a trading range for several days.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: recent daily bars have been range-bound rather than trending (mirrors R02-12).

complexity.reason: ‘trading range day’ needs the same design decision as ‘trend day’

candidates.name: NoMicroGapOverlap
candidates.quote: The bar after a bull trend bar has a low that is below the high of the bar before the bull trend bar.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: no micro gap forms around the trend bar — the following bar trades back into the range of the bar preceding it (mirrors R02-10).

complexity.reason: a three-bar structural test built on the trend-bar primitive

candidates.name: FirstPullbackTooEarly
candidates.quote: The first pullback occurs two bars after the reversal.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: a pullback shows up almost immediately after the breakout (mirrors R02-14's delayed-pullback strength sign).

complexity.reason: needs the breakout-start bar remembered as state

candidates.name: FirstPullbackTooLong
candidates.quote: The pullback extends for several bars.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: the first pullback runs long instead of resolving in one or two bars (mirrors R02-15).

complexity.reason: needs pullback-span detection

candidates.name: StalledResumptionLowerHigh
candidates.quote: The trend resumption after the pullback stalls and the market forms a lower high with a bear signal bar.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: the attempted resumption after the pullback fails to make a new high and instead prints a lower high with a bear signal bar.

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection to compare successive highs

candidates.name: BarelyClearsResistanceThenReverses
candidates.quote: The spike breaks above a resistance level like a swing high, a bear trend line, or a bull trend channel line by only a tick or so and then reverses down.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: the spike barely exceeds a resistance level before immediately reversing.
candidates.pseudocode: high[1] > resistanceLevel && high[1] - resistanceLevel <= barelyTicks * tickSize && close[0] < resistanceLevel

complexity.reason: resistanceLevel is a remembered swing high, trend line, or channel line

candidates.name: BarelyClearsMultipleLevelsWithoutBreaking
candidates.quote: The spike barely breaks above a single resistance level but pulls back before breaking above other levels that are just a little higher.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: the spike clears only the nearest of several nearby resistance levels and pulls back before reaching the next one.
candidates.pseudocode: high[1] > level1 && high[1] - level1 <= barelyTicks * tickSize && high[1] < level2 && close[0] < level1

complexity.reason: needs at least two remembered resistance levels

candidates.name: ScalpProfitNotAchievedBeforePullback
candidates.quote: A trader who bought on a stop above a prior swing high would not be able to make a scalper's profit before there was a pullback.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: price never travels far enough beyond the swing-high breakout to reach a scalp target before pulling back (mirrors R02-06's strength sign).
candidates.pseudocode: swingHigh = highest(high, swingLookback)[1]; highest(high, pullbackWindow) - swingHigh < scalpTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: needs a forward-looking window evaluated once the pullback is identified

candidates.name: PullbackBelowBreakoutPointNoGap
candidates.quote: The pullback falls below the breakout point. There are no gaps between the low of any bar and the high of the bar two bars earlier.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: the pullback trades below the breakout point, and the spike never formed one of the micro gaps that would otherwise mark it as strong.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] < breakoutPoint && !exists i in [0, lookback): low[i] > high[i + 2]

complexity.reason: combines a remembered breakout point with a windowed gap-absence scan

candidates.name: PullbackBelowSpikeStart
candidates.quote: The pullback falls below the low of the first bar of the spike.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: the pullback erases the entire spike, trading below where the spike began.

complexity.reason: spikeStartLow must persist as remembered state from the start of the spike

candidates.name: PullbackHitsBreakeven
candidates.quote: The pullback hits the breakeven stop.
candidates.description: Sign of weakness: the pullback trades back to the position's own entry price.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (breakout-failure signal; often coincides with a breakeven stop order)

complexity.reason: a single comparison against the position's entry price

candidates.name: BreakoutStrengthComposite
candidates.quote: the more of the following characteristics that a bull breakout has, the more likely the breakout will be strong
candidates.description: Composite named by Brooks himself: score a breakout by how many of the individual signs of strength (R02-01..R02-17) are present, and require at least a minimum count before treating the breakout as reliable.

complexity.reason: Brooks gives a checklist, not a weighting or a required count; picking minSignsRequired and whether to weight signs is a design decision

notes: This is exactly the kind of composite the mining brief invites: a named list whose members are already split into atomic candidates.

candidates.name: StrictBreakoutDefinition
candidates.quote: Strictly speaking, if the high of a bar is above the high of any prior bar or the low of the bar is below the low of any prior bar, it is a breakout of that bar.
candidates.description: Primitive: the loosest possible breakout test — a new high (or low) versus a very long lookback window, approximating ‘any prior bar’.

complexity.reason: a highest-high window; true ‘any prior bar’ would need the full data history, approximated with a large fixed lookback

candidates.name: SpikeMeasuredMoveOpenToClose
candidates.quote: When a breakout is that strong, it usually is followed by a channel and often leads to a measured move from the open of the first bar to the close of the final bar in the spike.
candidates.description: After a strong spike from bar s to bar e, project a measured move using the spike's open-to-close height (rather than its high-low range) added beyond the spike's close.
candidates.pseudocode: height = close[e] - open[s]; target = close[e] + height; high[0] >= target - toleranceTicks * tickSize

complexity.reason: the spike's start and end bars must persist as remembered state

notes: Distinct anchor from RP1-07/R08's high-low spike height; the dedup pass should keep both forms since Brooks uses each in different places.

candidates.name: ReversalWithoutTouchingResistanceIsStrongSign
candidates.quote: Whenever a market turns back down without touching a resistance level, the bears are very strong because they are not waiting for the resistance to be touched.
candidates.description: Filter: a reversal that begins before price even reaches a nearby remembered resistance level is a stronger with-trend signal than one that waits for the level to be tested.
candidates.pseudocode: highest(high, sinceSignalLookback) < resistanceLevel - untouchedTicks * tickSize && close[0] < open[0]

complexity.reason: needs a remembered resistance level and confirmation that price never reached it

candidates.name: FinalHourForcedLiquidationBreakout
candidates.quote: There is a special type of breakout that sometimes occurs on trend days in the final hour ... risk managers at trading firms are telling their traders who have been bottom picking that they are on the wrong side of the market and that they have to sell out of their positions at the market.
candidates.description: Filter/context: a fresh break to a new extreme in the final hour of a strong trend day is more likely forced liquidation than fresh conviction, and typically lacks follow-through.
candidates.pseudocode: barsRemainingInSession(sessionEndTime) <= finalHourBars && AlwaysInTrendContext == bearish && low[0] < lowest(low, channelLookback)[1]

complexity.reason: the institutional-liquidation motive has no bar-level signature beyond time-of-day and trend context

candidates.name: ThreePushChannelReversalSetup
candidates.quote: Channels often have three pushes before they correct, and this one did as well. The three pushes were bars 18, 25, and 36.
candidates.description: Filter/context: once a trend channel has made its third push (swing extreme) in the same direction, expect at least a reversal attempt or correction.
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter ahead of a countertrend or profit-taking decision)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection to count pushes within a channel

rejected.quote: As the first bar of the breakout bar is forming, it spends most of its time near its high and the pullbacks are small (less than a quarter of the height of the growing bar).
rejected.reason: requires intrabar tick-level price path data, which the engine does not have below the bar

rejected.quote: As the breakout bar is forming, it pulls back more than two-thirds of the height of the bar.
rejected.reason: requires intrabar tick-level price path data

rejected.quote: As the breakout bar is forming, it pulls back for at least a third of its height two or more times.
rejected.reason: requires intrabar tick-level price path data

rejected.quote: There is a sense of urgency. You feel like you have to buy but you want a pullback, yet it never comes.
There is a sense of confusion. You feel like you are not certain whether the breakout will succeed or fail.

chapter_summary: The chapter's core is two parallel checklists (signs of strength, signs of weakness) for a bull breakout, explicitly mirrored for bear breakouts; each bullet was split into its own atomic candidate (R02-01..R02-31) plus one composite (R02-32) naming the checklist itself, exactly as the mining brief anticipated. Three bullets requiring intrabar path data and two purely emotional bullets were rejected. The following chart-walkthrough narrative added a handful of new mechanizable ideas beyond the checklist: a strict any-prior-bar breakout definition, an open-to-close spike measured move, a 'reversal before touching resistance' strength booster, a final-hour forced-liquidation context filter, and a three-push channel reversal setup. Many measured-move and climax-counting ideas here duplicate RP1 and R08 and should be merged in the dedup pass.
